items.title: The Forbidden Library No. 2: The Voynich Manuscript
items.hook: An unknown script. Pages written in a lost tongue.
items.angle: Detailed breakdown of MS 408 held at Yale University's Beinecke Library.
items.why_now: Aligns with top historical archive interest.
facts: Located at Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, MS 408
Radiocarbon dated to the early 15th century between 1404 and 1438
Contains over 240 vellum folios with unreadable botanical illustrations
Acquired by antiquarian Wilfrid Voynich in 1912 in Italy
Resisted every modern cryptanalytic attempt for a century

items.title: 4 Lies You Believe About Medieval Witch Trials
items.hook: Everything you know about witch trials is a Victorian lie.
items.angle: Deconstructing modern misconceptions versus actual inquisitorial court records.
facts: The Malleus Maleficarum was published in 1486 by Heinrich Kramer
Torture was legally regulated and required judicial oversight in secular courts
Most accused in Iceland and Estonia during trials were actually men
Witches were rarely burned at the stake in England, hanging was standard
The 'Witches' Sabbath' was largely a construct of demonic projection theories
